risks.note: The MD&A THREATS section states India imports nearly 85% of its crude oil and large portions of its LPG and LNG, so global geopolitical conflicts directly trigger supply chain disruptions, soaring insurance/freight costs and domestic price spikes. It singles out Strait of Hormuz dependence - halted tankers, surging war-risk insurance premiums and demurrage charges - and 'import force majeure' from Middle East volatility. Expo's order book and its entire named bid pipeline sit inside refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser and green-ammonia projects, so a stalled or deferred customer capex cycle transmits straight to order inflow.
risks.risk: End-market dependence on India's oil & gas capex cycle, which is itself hostage to import dependency and shipping chokepoints

risks.note: The notes state the Company is principally engaged in metal fabrication and is managed as one entity governed by the same set of risks and return, hence there are no separate reportable segments under Ind AS 108. All manufacturing runs through one integrated facility at Murbad, Thane. There is no second plant, no subsidiary, associate or joint venture as at 31 March 2026, so a disruption at Murbad or a downturn in fabrication demand has no internal offset.
risks.risk: Single-activity, single-site concentration with no segment diversification

risks.note: The MD&A flags higher input costs from duties and inverted tariff structures for certain materials as an India-specific structural constraint. The Company's own timeline records that its 2003-2009 difficulties began with challenges in tendering and execution on an IOCL Panipat order following a sudden steel price surge and the absence of a price escalation clause, leading to a debt burden that was only resolved by a One Time Settlement in 2009. The risk is therefore demonstrated, not theoretical.
risks.risk: Fixed-price contracting exposure to input-cost inflation, with a realised precedent in the Company's own history

risks.note: The Chairman describes FY2025-26 as a challenging year with revenue at Rs 68.23 crore against Rs 114.74 crore in FY2024-25 - a project-execution business whose top line swings with the timing of a handful of large contracts. The order book cited at year-end is Rs 94 crore (the corporate overview separately cites Rs 122 crore including the ONGC win), so visibility rests on converting a small number of large orders and on the L1 tender positions actually being awarded.
risks.risk: Revenue lumpiness and a materially shrunken FY26 base against a modest order book

risks.note: The Chairman names IOCL, BPCL, ONGC, Reliance Industries and L&T as the client base, and the individual order milestones disclosed - Rs 25.62 crore from BPCL (2025), Rs 26.09 crore from IOCL (2025), Rs 44.66 crore from ONGC (2026) - are each large relative to annual revenue. Loss of prequalification with, or a capex pause at, any one of these buyers is material.
risks.risk: Customer concentration in a narrow set of PSU and large private counterparties

risks.note: The MD&A lists costly international certifications (ASME, CE, API, PED, etc.) among the domestic constraints Indian manufacturers face. Expo's competitive position depends on holding ISO 9001/14001/45001, the ASME 'U' Stamp and the National Board 'R' and 'NB' Stamps; these must be maintained and renewed, and a lapse would remove the Company from the tender lists it depends on.
risks.risk: Certification and compliance cost burden as a standing operating expense

risks.note: The MD&A explicitly names high logistics and infrastructure costs compared with leading manufacturing nations, relatively expensive industrial land and utilities in some regions, and limited investment in indigenous R&D compared with global competitors as constraints on Indian process plant machinery manufacturers - a persistent margin ceiling rather than a one-off.
risks.risk: Structural cost disadvantage versus leading manufacturing nations

risks.note: The MD&A states total employee strength stands at 43, so execution across projects in more than eleven states rests on a thin permanent team supplemented by contractors. The notes separately record that the Company has started making provision for gratuity and earned leave under Ind AS 19 but has not yet set aside any fund for those benefits, saying it is in the process and will contribute in the near future - an unfunded liability against a modest net worth.
risks.risk: Very small workforce and unfunded retirement obligations

currentContext.expansion: Expo's expansion is centred on deepening capability at its single integrated manufacturing facility at Murbad, Thane rather than on adding new sites. The order book cited at year-end is Rs 94 crore (the corporate overview separately cites Rs 122 crore including the ONGC win), so visibility rests on converting a small number of large orders and on the L1 tender positions actually being awarded.

risks.risk: Customer concentration in a narrow set of PSU and large private counterparties
risks.note: The Chairman names IOCL, BPCL, ONGC, Reliance Industries and L&T as the client base, and the individual order milestones disclosed - Rs 25.62 crore from BPCL (2025), Rs 26.09 crore from IOCL (2025), Rs 44.66 crore from ONGC (2026) - are each large relative to annual revenue. Loss of prequalification with, or a capex pause at, any one of these buyers is material.

risks.risk: Certification and compliance cost burden as a standing operating expense
risks.note: The MD&A lists costly international certifications (ASME, CE, API, PED, etc.) among the domestic constraints Indian manufacturers face. Expo's competitive position depends on holding ISO 9001/14001/45001, the ASME 'U' Stamp and the National Board 'R' and 'NB' Stamps; these must be maintained and renewed, and a lapse would remove the Company from the tender lists it depends on.

risks.risk: Structural cost disadvantage versus leading manufacturing nations
risks.note: The MD&A explicitly names high logistics and infrastructure costs compared with leading manufacturing nations, relatively expensive industrial land and utilities in some regions, and limited investment in indigenous R&D compared with global competitors as constraints on Indian process plant machinery manufacturers - a persistent margin ceiling rather than a one-off.

risks.risk: Very small workforce and unfunded retirement obligations
risks.note: The MD&A states total employee strength stands at 43, so execution across projects in more than eleven states rests on a thin permanent team supplemented by contractors. The notes separately record that the Company has started making provision for gratuity and earned leave under Ind AS 19 but has not yet set aside any fund for those benefits, saying it is in the process and will contribute in the near future - an unfunded liability against a modest net worth.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: Founded in 1982 as an LPG cylinder manufacturer at Murbad, Thane and pivoted to process plant equipment between 1992 and 2002, Expo today delivers integrated engineering solutions across the project lifecycle - design and detailed engineering, fabrication, on-site erection and installation, and maintenance and inspection. Core products are high-pressure vessels, heat exchangers, reactors, process columns, storage tanks and other custom-engineered process equipment, plus site-built fixed and floating roof storage tanks, mounded bullets and Horton spheres. capex_expansion.body: Expo's expansion is centred on deepening capability at its single integrated manufacturing facility at Murbad, Thane rather than on adding new sites. The Chairman states the Company has continued to invest in advanced fabrication technologies there, including modern welding systems and CNC profile cutting equipment, so that it can undertake increasingly sophisticated and larger-scale projects and serve the oil & gas, petrochemical, chemical, power, renewable energy and green hydrogen sectors. risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The MD&A THREATS section states India imports nearly 85% of its crude oil and large portions of its LPG and LNG, so global geopolitical conflicts directly trigger supply chain disruptions, soaring insurance/freight costs and domestic price spikes. It singles out Strait of Hormuz dependence - halted tankers, surging war-risk insurance premiums and demurrage charges - and 'import force majeure' from Middle East volatility. Expo's order book and its entire named bid pipeline sit inside refinery, petrochemical, fertiliser and green-ammonia projects, so a stalled or deferred customer capex cycle transmits straight to order inflow.
- The notes state the Company is principally engaged in metal fabrication and is managed as one entity governed by the same set of risks and return, hence there are no separate reportable segments under Ind AS 108. All manufacturing runs through one integrated facility at Murbad, Thane. There is no second plant, no subsidiary, associate or joint venture as at 31 March 2026, so a disruption at Murbad or a downturn in fabrication demand has no internal offset.
- The MD&A flags higher input costs from duties and inverted tariff structures for certain materials as an India-specific structural constraint. The Company's own timeline records that its 2003-2009 difficulties began with challenges in tendering and execution on an IOCL Panipat order following a sudden steel price surge and the absence of a price escalation clause, leading to a debt burden that was only resolved by a One Time Settlement in 2009. The risk is therefore demonstrated, not theoretical.
